correctness.rationale: Fourier transforming both conditional Fokker–Planck equations yields F_−=αF_+/(α+q²) and F_+(q)=½e^(−q²/2)(1+q²/α)^(−α/2), giving the cited known marginal. The Frullani transform identity writes its log characteristic function with strictly nonnegative Lévy density ν(x)=[(1+α/2)e^(−√α|x|)−e^(−√(2α)|x|)]/|x|; integrability near zero and infinity establishes infinite divisibility. Splitting off e^(−q²/2)(1+q²/α)^(−α/2) leaves a positive finite Lévy measure with mass log 2 by Frullani. Canonical one-dimensional self-decomposability is equivalent to monotonic k(r)=rν(r) on r>0; differentiating shows −k′(r)=√α[(1+α/2)e^(−√αr)−√2e^(−√(2α)r)]≥0 for all r iff α≥2(√2−1). Below threshold k rises near zero, excluding OU marginals. Above threshold h=−k′≥0 is integrable with symmetric total mass α and defines a CP-driven OU with Brownian sqrt2; integrating exp-damped jumps reconstructs ν. Independent quadrature checked exponent identities at α=.1, α_c,1,2,7. This proves equality of stationary *one-time* marginals only, not the switched path process.
